system.summary: Two different two-part numerical codes of about 1,700-1,850 groups (words, syllables, letters), groups separated by dots: Jefferson's Code No. 10 (Short) and Code No. 13 (Carmichael).
system.sibling_key: No key sheet is public for Code No. 10 or Code No. 13. key.tsv holds the 171 Code No. 10 values that Jefferson wrote over Short's groups. Code No. 11 (jefferson1787) does not fit Code No. 13.

solution.what: Catalogue 484 brief (Founders Online sweep): Short 26 Jul 1792 Code No. 10 (401, 1083, 401; 359, 199, 34, 724 undeciphered), Carmichael 14 Apr 1788 Code No. 13 (conjectural), T. Pinckney 28 Aug 1793 Code No. 16 (deciphered in part, 497 undeciphered).
Founders texts through the built-in browser (plain HTTP blocked); LoC item JSON gave mtj1 016_0998-1009 (Short) and 009_0223-0230 (Carmichael); master JPEGs from tile.loc.gov.
Short's private letter of 27 Jul 1792 (016_1010-1012) re-enciphers the paragraph with the same groups and no decoding: digits confirmed, no plaintext.
Code No. 10 values on 016_1007-1008 sorted by number to test alphabetical bracketing: no ordered run (two-part code); bracketing ruled out.
Carmichael's groups looked up in the Code No. 11 table rebuilt in jefferson1787: 597 = freedom, 223 = trouble there; Code No. 13 is a different code. Founders 'Code No. 13' = this letter only.

Search of the 39 Code No. 10 documents (Founders notes, six letters on the images, ~1,100 groups of 31 May 1793): 401, 1083, 359, 199, 34, 724 occur only in the 26 Jul 1792 passage; 'been' = 1700, not 401.
Subagent transcribed all 674 code groups of Short's 26 Jul 1792 letter with TJ's interlinear (511 groups under a TJ word).
reading.tsv measured: 737 groups, 728 with a reading (720 without conjectures), 9 open single-occurrence groups.

Split: Code No. 16 (Pinckney 28 Aug 1793 and the six letters of PR #399) moved to its own target, pinckney1793, one key per entry. This record keeps Short (Code No. 10) and Carmichael (Code No. 13). reading.tsv recounted for the two letters: 679 groups, 667 with a reading (511 under Jefferson's interlinear, 156 the editors'), 4 by conjecture only, 8 open; make_reading.py and make_key.py re-run and give the same files.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py) applying key.tsv to ct/short_17920726.txt: 674 groups, same order as texts/short_17920726_decryption.txt; 471 groups with a key.tsv value, 471 agree with the value or its other_readings; 99 continuation groups, 104 without a value (editors' readings, 7 open). key.tsv credits a word spread over several groups to its first group, so syllable groups carry several words: 1101 accept/acquainted/account (1101.660, 1101.119.844, 1101.1341: likely ac-), 689 conspicuous/consolation/consider (likely con-), 562 forms/inform/in-forming (form), 1259 re-medy/remaining (re-); 494 (from/without) and 534 (circumstances/honourable) stay unresolved. Carmichael 14 Apr 1788: v10 gives 0.974 only because capitalised conjectures [Maryland] [Massachusetts] are not turned into holes and 597 is a number; counting the 4 conjectures and 597 as holes over the 35 clear words gives 0.875, so read in part stands (recorded 0.0 counts the 5 code items only). No reading changed; images not re-read.

Project check of PR #570 (Brice Dudout): his script re-run: 674 groups of Short's letter in the order of the decryption, 471 with a key.tsv value, all agreeing. key.tsv credits a multi-group word to its first group, so 1101, 689, 562, 1259 carry several words (syllable values ac-, con-, form, re- likely); 494 and 534 unresolved. Carmichael: read_share kept at 0.0 (code items); the word figure with the conjectures as holes is 0.875; v10's 0.974 is an artefact. Nothing changed in key.tsv or the readings.

outcome.method_basis: The readings are Jefferson's interlinear decoding of Short's letter and the Jefferson Papers editors' printed decodings of both letters; the work transcribed every group, set Jefferson's values against the editors' text, and searched the sibling letters of each code for the open groups.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.tsv: 679 counted code groups of the two letters (Short 674, one struck group excluded; Carmichael 5), 667 with a reading, 4 more by conjecture only (counted unread), 8 open.

texts.label: William Short to Jefferson, The Hague, 26 Jul 1792 (Code No. 10)
texts.summary: Short's private complaint at being passed over for Paris in favour of Gouverneur Morris: Lafayette's mortification, the French diplomatic committee's wish to refuse Morris, and Short's preferences for a post (the Hague as resident, Spain as plenipotentiary) and for the grades of the American diplomatic establishment.

reading_review.note: The coded paragraphs read through as Short's sentences (Jefferson's interlinear on 511 groups, the editors' reading on the rest); two short holes: 401/1083/401 and 359 199 34 724.

texts.label: William Carmichael to Jefferson, Madrid, 14 Apr 1788 (Code No. 13)
texts.summary: A clear letter with five code numbers used as a test of his cypher: Maryland (twice), Massachusetts and the majority on the ratification of the Constitution; the last item (597) stays open. The read share of 0% counts only the five code groups: none has a value attested in another letter (four are context conjectures, 597 is open), and the clear text of the letter is not counted.

reading_review.note: Two sentences of clear text with four code names read by context (Maryland, Massachusetts, majority) and one open item (597).
